 ATP Finals Carlos Alcaraz v Flavio Cobolli: ATP Finals tennis group stage – live
 🎾 ATP Finals updates from the afternoon action in Turin
 🎾 Mail Katy | Kartal’s fightback against injury and abuse 
 LIVE  Updated  5m ago Katy Murrells Fri 20 Nov 2026 08.34 EST First published on Fri 20 Nov 2026 07.01 EST Share Key events 2h ago Preamble 
 Carlos Alcaraz returns a shot during his match against Flavio Cobolli. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters View image in fullscreen Carlos Alcaraz returns a shot during his match against Flavio Cobolli. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters Katy Murrells Fri 20 Nov 2026 08.34 EST First published on Fri 20 Nov 2026 07.01 EST Share Key events 2h ago Preamble 
 4m ago 08.34 EST First set: Alcaraz 4-2 Cobolli* (*denotes next server) 
 On the third point, Alcaraz – stretching and sliding and looking untroubled by that hamstring – finds a vicious angle to combat Cobolli, and it’s 40-0. Cobolli comes back for 40-15 and then 40-30 when Alcaraz nets a volley. So Alcaraz has come down a little from that stratospheric level of the opening few games. But Alcaraz then lets off a rocket of a forehand that clips the sideline and that’s the game.
 Share 9m ago 08.30 EST First set: Alcaraz* 3-2 Cobolli (*denotes next server) 
 Cobolli’s vibe is similar to Alcaraz’s – with his quick feet, superb shotmaking and showmanship – but he doesn’t quite have Alcaraz’s level of concentration and consistency. That’s the challenge for the 24-year-old Italian next year, if he wants to win the game’s biggest prizes. The French Open runner-up keeps his eye in in this game, though, nailing an unreturned serve down the T on game point to seal it to 15.
 View image in fullscreen Flavio Cobolli has trouble matching Carlos Alcaraz early on. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters Share Updated at  08.34 EST 12m ago 08.27 EST First set: Alcaraz 3-1 Cobolli* (*denotes next server) 
 Cobolli finds a few first serves to secure his first hold, to 30, and get his name on the scoreboard, having been bagelled in the second set of his 7-6, 6-0 defeat by Tiafoe on Wednesday. But Alcaraz, showing a perfect balance of aggression and control, claims another commanding hold to maintain his advantage. Already it’s showtime for Alcaraz and already it’s looking ominous for Cobolli.
 Share 17m ago 08.21 EST First set: Alcaraz 2-0 Cobolli* (*denotes next server) 
 15-0, 30-0, 40-0. Cobolli then raises the biggest cheer so far from his home crowd with a forehand return winner, and he’s holding his arms in the air as if he’s broken back, but it’s still only 40-15 and Alcaraz wraps up the game on the next point by stepping forward to the net and finishing things with a beautiful backhand volley. Injury? Pah! What injury?! Alcaraz has started exactly where he left off against Medvedev and Tiafoe and his outstanding late-season form looks set to continue.
 Share Updated at  08.23 EST 21m ago 08.18 EST Alcaraz breaks: Alcaraz* 1-0 Cobolli (*denotes next server) 
 Ready? Let’s play. Cobolli won eight straight points at start of his match against Tiafoe, before fading fast, and it’s a quick start here, as he rips a cross-court forehand winner for 15-0. But very soon it all falls apart, and Alcaraz has break points at 15-40. Alcaraz doesn’t take the first but he does the second, and that was a cheap concession from Cobolli. Alcaraz’s hamstring hasn’t even really been tested yet.
 Share 25m ago 08.13 EST Alcaraz is looking like a 43-year-old rather than a 23-year-old out there, with strapping on his left hamstring, tape on his right knee and an arm sleeve to protect his right wrist. These two have surprisingly met only once before, by the way, back in 2023 at the French Open, with Alcaraz winning in straight sets in the first round.
 Share 29m ago 08.09 EST Jamie Murray muses on Sky that Alcaraz most likely didn’t get out of bed this morning doing back flips, given his physical predicament . Alcaraz does win the coin flip though, and he elects to receive. He wants to test Cobolli’s nerves on serve.
 Share 32m ago 08.06 EST “Buongiorno!” emails Simon Wylie. “ Several people (from my own family) have commented on the level of pedantry to which I dragged everyone down yesterday with my Italian plural comment.” I could do with Simon translating right now, though, because there’s plenty being said over the stadium’s speakers but non capisco . There’s a nice embrace between Alcaraz and Cobolli before they walk on to court – these two are good friends who have trained together before – and it’s the home player, with a cheeky wink, who arrives first, before Alcaraz, held together by all his strapping, follows.
 Share 41m ago 07.58 EST In other news today: 
 Men’s tennis boosts prize money for players to more than $350m in major overhaul Read more Share 42m ago 07.57 EST Tumaini Carayol Leon Smith will step down from his role as Great Britain’s Davis Cup captain at the end of this month after 16 years in the position. Britain’s appearance in the Davis Cup Finals next week will mark his final competition.
 Smith has enjoyed one of the longest tenures as a Davis Cup captain in the sport’s history and the longest by a British Davis Cup captain. The highlight of his term was Britain’s historic Davis Cup triumph in 2015, a team also led by his childhood friend Andy Murray.
 Smith said: “It has been an enormous privilege to lead the team for so many years, and I feel now is the right time, both for me personally and for the team moving forwards.”
 Smith had been considering his resignation for some months and the LTA has already started planning for his successor, with the new Davis Cup captain expected to be announced in the coming weeks. Smith will continue his role as the LTA’s head of men’s tennis, which he took on at the same time that he became Davis Cup captain in 2010.
 Share 44m ago 07.55 EST Skupski’s also got next week’s Davis Cup Finals to look forward to, which will be Leon Smith’s final event as Britain’s captain , after the LTA announced today that he’s stepping down after 16 years in the role. Smith will be remembered, of course, for guiding the team to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years in 2015 – it’s not believed that Andy Murray, who spearheaded that win, is interested in taking over the role at this time.
 Share Updated at  07.56 EST 47m ago 07.52 EST Already today in the doubles, Britain’s Neal Skupski and his American partner Christian Harrison , the reigning Australian and US Open champions in a fine first season together, have snatched the last semi-final spot with a 7-6 (5), 6-4 win over Spain’s Marcel Granollers and Argentina’s Horacio Zeballos.
 Share 1h ago 07.34 EST Alcaraz is practising on an outside court at the moment. He’s got heavy strapping around that left hamstring, as well as tape on his right knee, and he’s barely got out of first gear yet, as he cautiously warms up. He’s hitting a lot closer to a match than he normally would, probably because he doesn’t want to risk the hamstring seizing up between practice and facing Cobolli.
 View image in fullscreen The scene right now. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters Share 1h ago 07.26 EST Share 1h ago 07.24 EST Share 1h ago 07.23 EST In the John McEnroe group yesterday, Alexander Zverev finished top with his third straight-sets win out of three , though Arthur Fils ( and his nuclear forehand ) made the world No 1 work for the 6-4, 7-6 victory, while Ben Shelton qualified for the semi-finals for the first time after seeing off the winless Rafael Jodar 7-6, 7-5.
 Zverev will now face the victor of tonight’s straight shoot-out between Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe, and Shelton will meet Alcaraz in a rematch of that US Open quarter-final. Yes please (though hopefully this one won’t finish at 3.30am …)
 Share 2h ago 07.04 EST And talking about Agassi: this is a lovely trip down memory lane of the 1990 season-ending final. 
 Share Updated at  07.06 EST 2h ago 07.01 EST Preamble
 Buongiorno ! With Carlos Alcaraz already guaranteed to finish top of the Ivan Lendl group after two straight-sets wins, the biggest jeopardy going into his match against the already-eliminated Flavio Cobolli is the state of his left hamstring. After picking up the injury against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday , Alcaraz had an MRI scan yesterday and was cleared to play on, so now we’ll get to see if he can still hit the absurd levels he did earlier this week.
 While Alcaraz is riding a late-season wave after his wrist injury-enforced summer hiatus, sweeping up titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris, Cobolli was reduced to tears after the 7-6, 6-0 loss to Frances Tiafoe that sealed his exit two days ago. The Italian – the only home player in the Jannik Sinner-less singles – said it was the saddest match of his career and that he felt he’d let the Turin crowd down on his ATP Finals debut. But Cobolli still described today’s meeting with Alcaraz – just the second of his career – as “a beautiful gift … I hope to annoy him as much as possible, even if it won’t be easy”.
 A description of Cobolli’s style – rapid feet, flashy shotmaking, great hands and effortless charisma – could of course be used for Alcaraz too, and it was actually training with Alcaraz a few years ago in Spain that flicked a switch in Cobolli and transformed his work ethic. This match represents a free shot for the French Open runner-up against a player he admires so much and gets on with so well, while for Alcaraz it’s a chance to test his hamstring with no pressure on the result.
 Alcaraz won’t take any unnecessary risks with the injury – he’s got the Davis Cup Finals to come next week too and he probably still has those missed four months at the back of his mind – but if he’s fit, yet another piece of tennis history is his for the taking. Having started his ATP season by becoming the youngest man to complete a career grand slam, he could end it by joining Agassi, Federer and Djokovic as only the fourth man in history to have won all four majors and the season finale. It’s so good to have him back; let’s hope this latest injury doesn’t force him away again.
 Play begins at: about 1pm GMT/2pm local time. Andiamo !
